lines.simpleEn: You are the giver who sustains every being.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਭ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਦਾਤਾਂ ਦੇਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਸਰਬੰ gives the address its inclusive reach, while ਦਾਤਾ names giving. The line praises the Divine rather than promising that every personal request will be granted.

lines.simpleEn: You know all that exists.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਾਰਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਕੁਝ ਜਾਣਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਗਿਆਤਾ names the knower, not merely a collection of information. Divine knowing here does not establish that any human interpreter or teacher knows another person completely.

lines.simpleEn: You are the light through which all things become manifest.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਭ ਨੂੰ ਪਰਗਟ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਚਾਨਣ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਭਾਨੇ is read here through radiance and manifestation. This is a working devotional reading of the image, not a scientific assertion about the physical production of light.

lines.simpleEn: You are the honour and greatness present throughout creation.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਾਰੀ ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਣ ਦਾ ਆਧਾਰ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਮਾਨੇ allows an honour-giving emphasis as well as being honoured by all. The selected explanation follows the former; the latter is praise with universal scope, not a survey of what every person believes.

lines.simpleEn: You are the life that sustains every living being.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਾਰੇ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਜੀਵਨ-ਸ਼ਕਤੀ ਦਾ ਆਧਾਰ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਪ੍ਰਾਣੰ carries life or life-breath language. The explanation addresses the source of life; it does not prescribe breath retention, a breathing method or a measure of spiritual worth.

lines.simpleEn: You are the refuge and protection of all.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਭ ਦਾ ਆਸਰਾ ਅਤੇ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਤ੍ਰਾਣੰ adds protection to the preceding life image. Devotional refuge does not imply that people cannot suffer or that practical care and protection are unnecessary.

lines.simpleEn: You are the One who experiences and enjoys all creation.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਾਰੀ ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਨੂੰ ਭੋਗਣ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੁਭਵ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਭੁਗਤਾ is provisionally read as the enjoyer or experiencer. A sustenance-related explanation also occurs in the consulted commentary. These emphases should not be collapsed into a claim that every human appetite is righteous.

lines.simpleEn: You are joined with all and present throughout everything.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਿਆ ਹੋਇਆ ਹੈਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਜੁਗਤਾ is read here as joined or connected. It completes the movement from life and protection to presence; it is not an instruction for a particular yoga exercise.

lines.simpleEn: You are the radiant Divine presence in all.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਭ ਵਿੱਚ ਚਮਕਦੀ ਰੱਬੀ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਦੇਵੰ can emphasise radiance or the One worthy of reverence. This explanation selects the radiant-presence sense while retaining the devotional force.

lines.simpleEn: You are the mystery within all that cannot be fully grasped.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਭ ਅੰਦਰ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਉਹ ਭੇਦ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਪੂਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਫੜਿਆ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
lines.nuance: ਭੇਵੰ brings mystery beside the preceding radiance. Being manifest in all and not being exhaustively understood are not treated here as mutually exclusive.

lines.simpleEn: You are the power of time and the ending of all finite life.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਮੇਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਨਾਸਵੰਤ ਜੀਵਨ ਦੇ ਅੰਤ ਦੀ ਸੱਤਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਕਾਲੇ retains the seriousness of time and death. An enduring-presence reading is also recorded in commentary; the main explanation does not quietly remove the ending image.

lines.simpleEn: You are the One who nurtures and sustains all.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਭ ਨੂੰ ਪਾਲਣ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਭਾਲਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਪਾਲੇ answers the preceding ending image with nurture. The two remain side by side; praise of the Divine as the end of life is not permission for a human being to destroy life.

lines.simpleEn: You are the primal reality with no beginning, beyond birth and without limit.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਦਾ ਮੁੱਢ ਹੈਂ ਪਰ ਆਪ ਮੁੱਢ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ, ਜਨਮ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਅਤੇ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਆਦਿ and ਅਨਾਦਿ distinguish being the origin of others from having an origin oneself. ਮੂਰਤਿ here is read as reality or presence, not as requiring an image or a bounded physical body.

lines.simpleEn: Honoured throughout existence, radiant and unfathomable, You are generous from the beginning.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਭ ਥਾਵਾਂ ਮਾਣਯੋਗ, ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ਮਾਨ ਅਤੇ ਅਗਾਧ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ; ਆਦਿ ਤੋਂ ਹੀ ਉਦਾਰ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਤ੍ਰਿਮਾਨ has readings involving honour in three realms or across three times. The main line keeps its comprehensive honour without deciding that difference. ਅਭੇਵ and ਉਦਾਰ retain mystery and generosity rather than becoming names of separate beings.

lines.simpleEn: You sustain all, bring all to dissolution, and are the end of every finite being.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਨੂੰ ਪਾਲਦਾ, ਸਭ ਨੂੰ ਸਮੇਟਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਹਰ ਨਾਸਵੰਤ ਜੀਵ ਦਾ ਅੰਤ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਪਾਲਕ, ਘਾਲਕ and ਕਾਲ must each remain visible. ਘਾਲਕ is selected in its dissolution sense here; a doing or bringing-into-action analysis is also noted in commentary. Neither reading grants human authority over life.

lines.simpleEn: You are present everywhere, unattached yet full of living richness.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਹਰ ਥਾਂ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੈਂ—ਨਿਰਲੇਪ ਵੀ ਅਤੇ ਰਸ ਨਾਲ ਭਰਪੂਰ ਵੀ।
lines.nuance: ਅਵਧੂਤ and ਰਿਸਾਲ hold detachment and richness of experience together. The source spells ਰਿਸਾਲ; this explanation does not replace it with another witness’s ਰਸਾਲ or turn detachment into neglect of relationships.

lines.simpleEn: No single name, place, lineage, form, colour or outline can contain You.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਕੋਈ ਇੱਕ ਨਾਮ, ਥਾਂ, ਜਾਤ, ਰੂਪ, ਰੰਗ ਜਾਂ ਰੇਖਾ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦੀ।
lines.nuance: The list denies limiting classifications. It does not forbid the names used in praise; the act of naming is held together with recognition that a name cannot exhaust what it addresses.

lines.simpleEn: You are the primal, generous presence, unborn and complete without remainder.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਆਦਿ ਪੁਰਖ, ਉਦਾਰ ਹਸਤੀ, ਜਨਮ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਅਤੇ ਸਰਬਪੂਰਨ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: The paired ਆਦਿ terms keep the primal sense in view. ਅਸੇਖ is provisionally read as complete or leaving nothing outside; it is not a numerical measurement of the Divine.

lines.simpleEn: No country or costume, shape or mark, and no binding attachment define You.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਕੋਈ ਦੇਸ, ਭੇਸ, ਰੂਪ, ਰੇਖਾ ਜਾਂ ਬੰਨ੍ਹਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਰਾਗ ਤੇਰੀ ਪਛਾਣ ਨੂੰ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰਦਾ।
lines.nuance: ਰਾਗ is read here as attachment or attraction rather than as the name of a musical raag. The surrounding list concerns limiting identities, not a rejection of music or of human cultural belonging.

lines.simpleEn: Your loving presence reaches here and there, in every direction and between them.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰੀ ਪ੍ਰੇਮਮਈ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਇੱਥੇ-ਉੱਥੇ, ਹਰ ਦਿਸ਼ਾ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਚਕਾਰਲੀਆਂ ਦਿਸ਼ਾਵਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੈ।
lines.nuance: ਦਿਸਾ ਵਿਸਾ expands the spatial image, while ਅਨੁਰਾਗ introduces love after the preceding denial of binding attachment. The contrast should not be flattened into an instruction to have no affection.

lines.simpleEn: You are beyond a limiting name or desire, and no single dwelling can be assigned to You.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸੀਮਤ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਨਾਮ ਅਤੇ ਕਾਮਨਾ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈਂ; ਤੇਰਾ ਕੋਈ ਇੱਕ ਨਿਸ਼ਚਿਤ ਟਿਕਾਣਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
lines.nuance: The line concerns how the Divine is apprehended: without a confining name, desire or home. It is not a statement that people should abandon their names, ordinary needs or secure housing.

lines.simpleEn: You are praised as worthy of honour everywhere and always.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਥਾਵਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਦਾ ਮਾਣ ਦੇ ਯੋਗ ਮੰਨਿਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਮਾਨ occurs repeatedly with universal, spatial and enduring force. The line is an act of praise, not evidence that all people actually agree about religion.

lines.simpleEn: Your reality is One, yet You are encountered through the many forms You have made.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰੀ ਹਸਤੀ ਇੱਕ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਤੇਰੇ ਰਚੇ ਅਨੇਕ ਰੂਪਾਂ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਤੇਰੀ ਝਲਕ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ।
lines.nuance: ਏਕ and ਅਨੇਕ create the central contrast. The statement does not rank particular bodies or communities as more Divine than others, nor does it prove any person’s claim to be a Divine incarnation.

lines.simpleEn: You unfold the wondrous play of many forms; when that play is gathered in, the One remains.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਅਨੇਕ ਰੂਪਾਂ ਦੀ ਅਚਰਜ ਖੇਡ ਰਚਦਾ ਹੈਂ; ਖੇਡ ਸਮੇਟੇ ਜਾਣ ਉੱਤੇ ਵੀ ਇੱਕ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: The repeated ਖੇਲ is a poetic image for manifestation and its ending. ਅਖੇਲ is difficult to compress into English; the draft preserves wonder rather than claiming a technical cosmological sequence. Calling creation play must not trivialise suffering.

lines.simpleEn: Neither heavenly beings nor the Vedas and other sacred books can fully fathom Your mystery.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਦੇਵਤੇ, ਵੇਦ ਅਤੇ ਹੋਰ ਧਰਮਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਕਿਤਾਬਾਂ ਵੀ ਤੇਰਾ ਭੇਦ ਪੂਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾਣ ਸਕਦੇ।
lines.nuance: ਕਤੇਬ extends the reference beyond the Vedas to other scriptural books. The line sets a limit on complete comprehension; it does not tell the reader to mock other traditions or stop learning.

lines.simpleEn: Without a fixed form, colour, caste or lineage, by what outward description could You be completely known?
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰਾ ਕੋਈ ਨਿਸ਼ਚਿਤ ਰੂਪ, ਰੰਗ, ਜਾਤ ਜਾਂ ਕੁਲ ਨਹੀਂ; ਕਿਸ ਬਾਹਰੀ ਪਛਾਣ ਨਾਲ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਪੂਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਜਾਣੀਏ?
lines.nuance: The question turns from a list of absent classifications toward the problem of knowing. ਜੇਬ is provisionally treated as manner or description here; this should not be mistaken for the modern Punjabi word for a pocket.

lines.simpleEn: You have no parents or lineage and are not subject to birth or death.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰੇ ਮਾਤਾ-ਪਿਤਾ ਜਾਂ ਕੁਲ ਨਹੀਂ; ਤੂੰ ਜਨਮ ਅਤੇ ਮਰਨ ਦੇ ਅਧੀਨ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: This contrasts Divine existence with inherited identity and mortality. It is not a judgment against parenthood, family ties, birth, ageing or a person’s bodily life.

lines.simpleEn: Your power moves throughout every direction, and the three worlds acknowledge You.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰੀ ਸੱਤਾ ਚਹੁੰ ਪਾਸੇ ਵਰਤਦੀ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਤਿੰਨੇ ਲੋਕ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਮੰਨਦੇ ਹਨ।
lines.nuance: ਚੱਕ੍ਰ ਬੱਕ੍ਰ is retained as a difficult movement or ordering image, not silently reduced to a familiar modern phrase. The draft gives its broad contextual force; precise grammar and the source’s ਚਤੁਰ ਚੱਕ form still need qualified review.

lines.simpleEn: Across the fourteen worlds, creation is pictured repeating Your praise.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਚੌਦਾਂ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਾਰੀ ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਤੇਰਾ ਜਾਪ ਕਰਦੀ ਦਿਖਾਈ ਗਈ ਹੈ।
lines.nuance: The fourteen worlds belong to the poem’s inherited cosmic vocabulary. The draft reads their comprehensive devotional force; it does not present them as a measured astronomical count.

lines.simpleEn: You are the primal Divine presence without beginning, the One who established all that exists.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਆਦਿ ਦੇਵ ਅਤੇ ਮੁੱਢ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹਸਤੀ ਹੈਂ; ਸਭ ਦੀ ਥਾਪਣਾ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਆਦਿ and ਅਨਾਦਿ again distinguish the origin of creation from an origin imposed on the Divine. The repeated ਥਾਪ forms emphasise establishing rather than a human act of building an object.

lines.simpleEn: You are supreme and pure, complete in presence and without limit.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਪਰਮ ਅਤੇ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ ਹੈਂ; ਤੇਰੀ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਸਰਬਪੂਰਨ ਅਤੇ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਹੈ।
lines.nuance: ਰੂਪ, ਮੂਰਤਿ and ਪੁਰਖ are read together as descriptions of Divine reality. Their presence here does not require a fixed physical outline after earlier stanzas deny such limits.

lines.simpleEn: Self-existent, You fashioned the whole universe and are its maker and dissolver.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਤੋਂ ਹੈਂ; ਸਾਰਾ ਵਿਸ਼ਵ ਰਚਣ, ਘੜਨ ਅਤੇ ਸਮੇਟਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਸੁਯੰਭਵ is read as self-existent, with no prior maker. ਗੜਨ and ਭੰਜਨ retain making and dissolution as distinct acts. The wording is devotional cosmology, not a scientific account of how the universe developed.

lines.simpleEn: Beyond time and death, endowed with power, You are the timeless presence not confined to a country.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਕਾਲ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ, ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਨਾਲ ਭਰਪੂਰ ਅਤੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਦੇਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਾ ਹੋਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਅਦੇਸ is selected as not limited to a particular place. An address of salutation is another recorded reading. ਕਾਲ ਹੀਨ and ਅਕਾਲ must not be turned into a promise of bodily immortality for the reader.

lines.simpleEn: You are the ground of dharam, free from delusion, beyond material confinement, sight and outward guise.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਧਰਮ ਦਾ ਆਧਾਰ, ਭਰਮ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ, ਭੌਤਿਕ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ, ਅਲੱਖ ਅਤੇ ਭੇਸ ਤੋਂ ਮੁਕਤ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਅਭੂਤ is provisionally read as beyond material or elemental confinement, alongside the unseeable and guiseless terms. Incomparability is another commentary emphasis; the list should not be compressed to only one quality.

lines.simpleEn: No bodily adornment, colour, caste, lineage or limiting name can define You.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਰੀਰਕ ਸਿੰਗਾਰ, ਰੰਗ, ਜਾਤ, ਕੁਲ ਜਾਂ ਸੀਮਤ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਨਾਮ ਤੇਰੀ ਹੱਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਦੱਸ ਸਕਦਾ।
lines.nuance: ਅੰਗ ਰਾਗ is provisionally grouped as bodily colour or adornment. Other analyses separate body and attachment. Neither makes ordinary bodily appearance a measure of anyone’s spiritual worth.

lines.simpleEn: You humble pride, overcome wickedness, and act as the giver of liberation.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਹੰਕਾਰ ਤੋੜਦਾ, ਦੁਸ਼ਟਤਾ ਦਾ ਨਾਸ ਕਰਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਮੁਕਤੀ ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਗਰਬ and ਦੁਸਟ distinguish pride from harmful conduct, while ਮੁਕਤਿ adds liberation. ਕਾਮ is read as work or function in this phrase, not automatically as the desire sense found in other contexts.

lines.simpleEn: Your own reality is unfathomably deep, beyond complete praise: the One, present yet unattached.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰਾ ਆਪਣਾ ਸਰੂਪ ਅਗਾਧ ਹੈ; ਪੂਰੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ, ਇੱਕ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਰਲੇਪ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਅਮੀਕ retains depth, while ਅਨਉਸਤਤਿ points to the limits of praise. Saying that praise cannot be complete does not make the praise being offered meaningless.

lines.simpleEn: You humble pride and gather all into dissolution, the primal reality that was never born.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਹੰਕਾਰ ਤੋੜਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਨੂੰ ਸਮੇਟਦਾ ਹੈਂ; ਸਭ ਦਾ ਮੁੱਢ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਆਪ ਜਨਮ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: The line pairs the breaking of pride with the dissolution of all, then contrasts those changes with ਅਸੂਤ, not born. Human destruction is not authorised by the Divine title.

lines.simpleEn: Not confined to bodily limbs or a limited personal self, You remain unbroken, One and boundless.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਰੀਰ ਦੇ ਅੰਗਾਂ ਜਾਂ ਸੀਮਤ ਵਿਅਕਤੀਗਤ ਹਸਤੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੱਝਿਆ ਨਹੀਂ; ਅਟੁੱਟ, ਇੱਕ ਅਤੇ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਅਨਾਤਮ is interpretively difficult. This draft selects freedom from a limited personal self; unmanifest or non-self-interested emphases also occur in commentary. It is not a declaration that the Divine is lifeless, nor a final identification with another tradition’s technical doctrine.

lines.simpleEn: You are capable of all, the power that brings all to an end, and the sustainer of everyone.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਕੁਝ ਕਰਨ ਦੇ ਸਮਰੱਥ, ਸਭ ਦਾ ਅੰਤ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਨੂੰ ਪਾਲਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਲਾਇਕ is selected in the capable or worthy sense; a giver-of-life interpretation is also recorded. ਘਾਇਕ and ਪ੍ਰਤਿਪਾਰ keep ending and nurture together rather than allowing one to erase the other.

lines.simpleEn: You reach throughout all, bring all to an end, and cannot be confined to any outward guise.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਤੱਕ ਪਹੁੰਚਦਾ, ਸਭ ਦਾ ਅੰਤ ਕਰਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਬਾਹਰੀ ਭੇਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੱਝਦਾ।
lines.nuance: ਗੰਤਾ is provisionally read through going or reaching; ਹੰਤਾ retains ending or destruction. ਅਨਭੇਖ concerns non-confinement to an appearance. These are distinct descriptions rather than three versions of invisibility.

lines.simpleEn: No collection of sacred teachings can fully describe Your form, colour or outline.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਾਰੇ ਸ਼ਾਸਤਰ ਵੀ ਤੇਰੇ ਰੂਪ, ਰੰਗ ਜਾਂ ਰੇਖਾ ਦਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਵਰਣਨ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦੇ।
lines.nuance: The line names the limits of exhaustive description. It does not imply that sacred study has no value or that a teacher’s unsupported assertion should replace careful learning.

lines.simpleEn: The revered Vedas and Puranas continually say that no description reaches Your final limit.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਮੰਨੇ ਹੋਏ ਵੇਦ ਅਤੇ ਪੁਰਾਣ ਵੀ ਸਦਾ ਆਖਦੇ ਹਨ ਕਿ ਤੇਰੀ ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਹੱਦ ਬਿਆਨ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦੀ।
lines.nuance: ਨੇਤਿ is associated with the not-this, not-that way of refusing a final identification. The draft gives its limiting-description force without pretending one English formula resolves every philosophical usage.

lines.simpleEn: Even countless sacred texts cannot make the mind contain You completely.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਅਣਗਿਣਤ ਸਿਮ੍ਰਿਤੀਆਂ, ਪੁਰਾਣ ਅਤੇ ਸ਼ਾਸਤਰ ਵੀ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਮਨ ਦੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਪਕੜ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਲਿਆ ਸਕਦੇ।
lines.nuance: ਕੋਟਿ intensifies the scale. The point concerns the limits of mental containment, not a numerical ban on reading or an instruction to abandon reasoning.

lines.simpleEn: Your abundant virtues are generous and uplifting.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰੇ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਦਾ ਭੰਡਾਰ ਉਦਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਉੱਚਾ ਚੁੱਕਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਹੈ।
lines.nuance: ਗੁਨ ਗਨ brings virtues together as an abundance. The draft retains ਉਦਾਰ as generosity or nobility rather than treating every quality mentioned in the poem as an ordinary human possession.

lines.simpleEn: Your greatness has no reachable boundary.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰੀ ਮਹਿਮਾ ਦੀ ਕੋਈ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਸਕਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਹੱਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ।
lines.nuance: ਅਪਾਰ keeps the image of no far shore or limit. This is devotional praise rather than a measurable quantity.

lines.simpleEn: Your seat and abiding presence cannot be broken.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰਾ ਆਸਣ ਅਤੇ ਸਦਾ ਕਾਇਮ ਰਹਿਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਅਟੁੱਟ ਹੈ।
lines.nuance: ਆਸਨ provides a seat or throne image; existence or abiding presence is a broader commentary reading. The line does not prescribe a posture or certify any human throne as permanent.

lines.simpleEn: No bodily comparison can contain Your beauty and praise.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਕਿਸੇ ਸਰੀਰਕ ਤੁਲਨਾ ਨਾਲ ਤੇਰੀ ਸੁੰਦਰਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਉਸਤਤ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੰਨ੍ਹੀ ਜਾ ਸਕਦੀ।
lines.nuance: ਉਪਮਾ ਅਨੰਗ is not reduced to a single settled gloss. The draft selects praise beyond bodily comparison; a surpassing-beauty emphasis is also attested. This is not a rule for judging human attractiveness.

lines.simpleEn: Your light reveals itself rather than borrowing its source from another.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰਾ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਤੋਂ ਹੈ; ਉਹ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਤੋਂ ਉਧਾਰ ਲਿਆ ਚਾਨਣ ਨਹੀਂ।
lines.nuance: ਅਨਭਉ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ is selected in a self-revealing or self-luminous sense. Experientially disclosed spiritual understanding is another commentary emphasis. The line does not require a visual phenomenon or a particular meditative experience.

lines.simpleEn: Through night and day, You remain undiminished and imperishable.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਰਾਤ-ਦਿਨ ਤੂੰ ਅਵਿਨਾਸ਼ੀ ਅਤੇ ਸਦਾ ਕਾਇਮ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਨਿਸ ਦਿਨ gives continual scope to ਅਨਾਸ. It is the Divine being addressed, not a promise that a person who recites will escape ageing, illness or death.

lines.simpleEn: You are praised through the heroic image of far-reaching arms.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਲੰਮੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਦੂਰ ਤੱਕ ਪਹੁੰਚਦੀਆਂ ਭੁਜਾਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਵੀਰ-ਚਿੱਤਰ ਨਾਲ ਸਲਾਹਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ।
lines.nuance: ਆਜਾਨ ਬਾਹੁ uses the traditional long-armed image of majesty. It stands alongside earlier denials of bodily confinement. A command or authority interpretation also occurs; the image should not be turned into a measured anatomy of the Divine.

lines.simpleEn: You are the sovereign above every sovereign.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਾਰੇ ਸ਼ਾਹਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚਾ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਸਾਹਾਨ ਸਾਹੁ intensifies sovereignty. The retained source spelling is not replaced with ਸ਼ਾਹਾਨ ਸ਼ਾਹੁ. The title is not a statement about breathing and does not give any human sovereign absolute authority.

lines.simpleEn: Every ruler’s authority stands beneath Yours.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਹਰ ਰਾਜੇ ਦੀ ਸੱਤਾ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚੀ ਤੇਰੀ ਸੱਤਾ ਹੈ।
lines.nuance: ਰਾਜਾਨ ਰਾਜ repeats a rank to point beyond finite rank. It does not endorse a particular monarchy or give a ruler permission to claim Divine status.

lines.simpleEn: You are the light beyond all suns and their brilliance.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਾਰੇ ਸੂਰਜਾਂ ਦੇ ਚਾਨਣ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਪਰਮ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਭਾਨਾਨ ਭਾਨ uses solar radiance as praise. The wording is not a model of stellar energy, a count of suns or a claim that a particular astronomical event proves an interpretation.

lines.simpleEn: You are the Divine whom even the gods revere.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਦੇਵਤੇ ਵੀ ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਨ, ਉਹ ਪਰਮ ਦੇਵ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਦੇਵਾਨ ਦੇਵ places recognised heavenly powers within the wider praise of the One. The line does not ask the reader to demean people who describe divinity differently.

lines.simpleEn: Your praise points toward greatness beyond measure.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਮਹਾਨਤਾ ਵੱਲ ਇਸ਼ਾਰਾ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।
lines.nuance: ਉਪਮਾ ਮਹਾਨ completes the sequence by naming the greatness expressed in praise. Words point toward that greatness without becoming a complete inventory of it.

lines.simpleEn: You are the sovereign even above the heavenly sovereigns.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਦੇਵਤਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਰਾਜਿਆਂ ਤੋਂ ਵੀ ਉੱਚਾ ਰਾਜਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਇੰਦ੍ਰਾਨ ਇੰਦ੍ਰ invokes Indra as a title or image of heavenly sovereignty. The line subordinates that grandeur to the One rather than identifying a contemporary person as a heavenly king.

lines.simpleEn: You are higher than the highest.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਉੱਚਿਆਂ ਤੋਂ ਵੀ ਉੱਚਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: This selects the Persian-derived exalted sense associated with ਬਾਲਾ and the consulted commentary. Other translations choose the smallest or the child among children. These are materially different readings, so the alternative is retained rather than silently blended into the main line.

lines.simpleEn: You are present even as the poorest among the poor.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਗਰੀਬਾਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਗਰੀਬ ਦੇ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਤੂੰ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਰੰਕਾਨ ਰੰਕ interrupts the preceding language of elevated rank with poverty and low status. The explanation recognises dignity in those overlooked; it does not romanticise deprivation or suggest withholding practical help.

lines.simpleEn: You are beyond death itself, the ending of every power to end.
lines.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਮੌਤ ਤੋਂ ਵੀ ਪਰੇ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ; ਕਾਲ ਦਾ ਵੀ ਕਾਲ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
lines.nuance: ਕਾਲਾਨ ਕਾਲ takes the repeated-rank pattern to time and death. It is praise of the One, not a promise of human immortality or a reason to disregard the value of life.

studies.simpleEn: Giving, knowing, illumination and honour are brought together by the repeated word for all. The chhand moves attention away from a private claim on the Divine and toward an address that leaves no being outside its scope.
studies.simplePa: ਦਾਤ ਦੇਣਾ, ਜਾਣਨਾ, ਚਾਨਣ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਣ—ਇਹ ਚਾਰ ਗੱਲਾਂ ਸਰਬੰ ਦੀ ਦੁਹਰਾਈ ਨਾਲ ਇਕੱਠੀਆਂ ਹੁੰਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਛੰਦ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਕੇਵਲ ਆਪਣੇ ਲਈ ਮੰਨਣ ਦੀ ਥਾਂ ਸਭ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਾਂਝੇ ਆਧਾਰ ਵਜੋਂ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Hear the four different actions within the repeated universal address.
study.closeReading: Every line begins with ਸਰਬੰ, but the word following it changes. Giving concerns what is received; knowing concerns what is understood; radiance concerns what becomes apparent; honour concerns worth and greatness. Reading only the repeated opening would miss these differences. Reading only the four endings would miss their shared reach. The short lines therefore offer a practice in keeping particular qualities and universal scope together. In the final line, the direction of honour can be read in more than one way: honour bestowed throughout creation, or honour directed toward the Divine. Keep the selected explanation visible without turning a poetic universal into a claim that everyone holds the same beliefs.
words: all; the inclusive reach repeated in every line
radiance or making manifest in this working reading
honour or greatness; the direction of honour has alternative readings
study.care: These are original educational explanations, not an approved literal translation. Universal giving is not a guarantee of possessions; universal honour does not erase differences in human belief.
study.reflection: Consider someone whose work usually goes unnoticed. What would it mean to recognise their dignity without expecting anything in return?
study.teachBack: Name the four qualities after ਸਰਬੰ and explain the two directions in which the final honour image can be read.

studies.simpleEn: The repeated address includes life, shelter, experience and connected presence. Its movement is relational: the Divine is praised not only as a distant protector but also as present throughout the life that is being protected.
studies.simplePa: ਇੱਥੇ ਜੀਵਨ, ਆਸਰਾ, ਅਨੁਭਵ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜੀ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਹੈ। ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਦੂਰੋਂ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਨਹੀਂ, ਸਗੋਂ ਉਸ ਜੀਵਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੀ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਆਧਾਰ ਵਜੋਂ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Follow the progression from life to protection to shared presence.
study.closeReading: ਪ੍ਰਾਣੰ and ਤ੍ਰਾਣੰ sound close, yet they perform different work: life is followed by its shelter. The next pair changes the relationship again, introducing experience or enjoyment and then connection. This structure keeps the four short statements from becoming interchangeable slogans. The final ਜੁਗਤਾ gathers them into an image of presence with all. In reflection, distinguish the poem’s address to the Divine from a promise about what must happen to a particular person. The words can sustain gratitude and care without denying vulnerability. The enjoyer reading of ਭੁਗਤਾ remains a working choice; a nourishment-related interpretation should stay available for qualified review rather than being silently dismissed.
words: enjoyer or experiencer in the selected reading
study.care: Life-breath imagery is not a breathing prescription. Protection is devotional language, not immunity from harm. Human needs for safety, nourishment and care remain real.
study.reflection: What act of care could make the word protection concrete for someone who is vulnerable today?
study.teachBack: Explain why ਪ੍ਰਾਣੰ and ਤ੍ਰਾਣੰ are not the same word, then describe how ਜੁਗਤਾ changes the sense of the whole stanza.

studies.simpleEn: Radiance stands beside mystery, and the ending of life stands beside nurture. The chhand asks the reader to hold each pair together rather than reduce the Divine to only what is visible, pleasant or easily explained.
studies.simplePa: ਚਾਨਣ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਭੇਦ ਅਤੇ ਜੀਵਨ ਦੇ ਅੰਤ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਪਾਲਣਾ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਛੰਦ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਨੂੰ ਕੇਵਲ ਦਿਸਣ ਵਾਲੀ, ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ਜਾਂ ਸੌਖੀ ਵਿਆਖਿਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੰਨ੍ਹਣ ਦੀ ਥਾਂ ਇਹ ਜੋੜੇ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਸੁਣਨ ਲਈ ਕਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Notice the paired contrasts without cancelling either side.
study.closeReading: The first two lines place ਦੇਵੰ and ਭੇਵੰ in a close sound relationship. Light can disclose a presence without making its depth fully available to explanation. The last two lines use a similarly close sound relationship between ਕਾਲੇ and ਪਾਲੇ, placing an ending beside continued nourishment. These pairs invite careful reading rather than an easy resolution of every difficulty. A reader may find one half of a pair more comfortable than the other; the text nevertheless keeps both. The movement from mystery to time and nurture also sets up the longer descriptions that follow at Chhand 79. None of this makes grief unreal or turns human violence into a spiritual act.
words: time or death; an enduring-presence reading is also attested
study.care: The selected meanings remain provisional. Do not use the stanza to explain away another person’s grief, to claim knowledge of why a death occurred, or to justify harm.
study.reflection: Which is harder for you to acknowledge: that something may be present but mysterious, or that life includes both nurture and loss?
study.teachBack: Describe the two pairs and explain why interpreting ਪਾਲੇ does not require deleting the force of ਕਾਲੇ.

studies.simpleEn: The Rooaal heading introduces longer lines that join several descriptions at once. Origin without a beginning, universal honour, nurture and dissolution, and presence without attachment are brought into a single sustained address.
studies.simplePa: ਰੂਆਲ ਛੰਦ ਦੀ ਸਿਰਲੇਖੀ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਲੰਮੀਆਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਕਈ ਗੁਣ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਸਭ ਦਾ ਮੁੱਢ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਆਪ ਮੁੱਢ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਰਹਿਣਾ, ਸਭ ਥਾਂ ਮਾਣ, ਪਾਲਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਤ, ਤੇ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਨਿਰਲੇਪ ਰਹਿਣਾ—ਇਹ ਇੱਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Read each long line in meaningful phrases without changing the stored verse boundaries.
study.closeReading: The separate heading marks a change in poetic form; it is not a fifth verse. Within the first long line, ਆਦਿ and ਅਨਾਦਿ make a deliberate distinction between being the origin and being originated. The second line combines honour, radiance, mystery and generosity. The third refuses to isolate sustaining life from the fact that finite life ends. The fourth then joins presence everywhere with non-attachment and richness. These tensions give the stanza its depth. Read slowly enough to notice each term, but do not split the frozen four-line source into invented numbered lines. The word ਤ੍ਰਿਮਾਨ remains open to more than one threefold explanation, so the main teaching does not present one as settled.
words: unattached or detached in this context
rich in rasa or living savour; spelling retained
study.care: The metre label is structural metadata. The threefold honour reading and the sense of ਘਾਲਕ require qualified review. Dissolution is attributed to the Divine, not to a person seeking power.
study.reflection: How might non-attachment allow you to care more freely, rather than care less?
study.teachBack: Explain the distinction between ਆਦਿ and ਅਨਾਦਿ, identify all three actions in the third line, and say why the heading is not counted as a verse.

studies.simpleEn: The stanza first removes the boundaries by which people usually identify something, then speaks of loving presence everywhere. Being beyond a particular name or place does not mean being absent, and freedom from binding attachment does not mean lovelessness.
studies.simplePa: ਛੰਦ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਉਹ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਹਟਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਅਸੀਂ ਕਿਸੇ ਦੀ ਪਛਾਣ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਾਂ, ਫਿਰ ਹਰ ਥਾਂ ਪ੍ਰੇਮਮਈ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਕਿਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਨਾਮ ਜਾਂ ਥਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੋਣਾ ਗੈਰਹਾਜ਼ਰ ਹੋਣਾ ਨਹੀਂ; ਬੰਨ੍ਹਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਰਾਗ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੋਣਾ ਬੇਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਹੋਣਾ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: Distinguish freedom from limiting identity from absence of loving presence.
study.closeReading: The opening list moves through name, location, lineage and visible description. The next line changes direction, affirming primal presence, generosity, birthlessness and completeness. The third returns to limits, including country, clothing and attachment. Finally the fourth opens outward into every direction with ਅਨੁਰਾਗ. The poem therefore does not simply strip away everything and leave an empty statement. It moves from what cannot confine the Divine toward how love is present throughout existence. The juxtaposition of ਰਾਗ and ਅਨੁਰਾਗ deserves particular attention: a rejection of binding attachment need not be a rejection of affection. This is a reading of the stanza’s movement, not an instruction to abandon family or erase cultural identity.
words: complete or without remainder in this working reading
study.care: No fixed identity is being declared spiritually inferior. The text’s Divine description must not become pressure on a person to reject family, clothing, ethnicity or needed human connection.
study.reflection: Notice a label you use for someone. What might you understand better by remembering that the person is more than that label?
study.teachBack: Explain why the first line can deny a limiting name while the poem still uses names, and distinguish ਰਾਗ from ਅਨੁਰਾਗ in this setting.

studies.simpleEn: The first half refuses to confine the Divine to a name or home while extending honour everywhere. The second half places the One beside the many: varied appearances do not exhaust or divide the reality being praised.
studies.simplePa: ਪਹਿਲੀਆਂ ਦੋ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਨਾਮ ਜਾਂ ਟਿਕਾਣੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੰਨ੍ਹਣ ਤੋਂ ਇਨਕਾਰ ਕਰਦੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਉਸ ਦਾ ਮਾਣ ਹਰ ਥਾਂ ਮੰਨਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਅਖੀਰ ਦੀਆਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਇੱਕ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੇਕ ਨੂੰ ਨਾਲ ਰੱਖਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ: ਅਨੇਕ ਰੂਪ ਉਸ ਇੱਕ ਹਸਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਮੁਕਾ ਜਾਂ ਵੰਡ ਨਹੀਂ ਦਿੰਦੇ।

study.focus: Track the movement from no fixed dwelling to many appearances and the remaining One.
study.closeReading: The stanza begins by refusing the ordinary ways of locating a person: a particular name, desire or home. It then repeats honour across all places and times. The final pair provides a positive image rather than leaving only negation: ਏਕ ਮੂਰਤਿ and ਅਨੇਕ ਦਰਸਨ place oneness and multiplicity beside each other. The last line uses the language of play to describe the unfolding and gathering of forms. This need not mean that the One first stops being one and later becomes one again; the teaching can distinguish changing appearances from their enduring ground. Keep this as a reflective reading of the wording, not a final decision about every philosophical question the stanza raises.
words: play; here an image for the unfolding of creation
study.care: The image of play neither makes suffering unreal nor licenses indifference. The explanation is not an endorsement of an individual’s claim to supernatural identity.
study.reflection: When you meet people whose lives differ from yours, what might it mean to recognise shared worth without pretending their differences do not matter?
study.teachBack: Explain how ਏਕ and ਅਨੇਕ work together, and why the final play image is not a reason to dismiss someone’s suffering.

studies.simpleEn: The stanza asks how the unlimited can be known through limited descriptions. Scriptures, visible marks and family origins cannot provide a complete boundary around the Divine; the final line turns outward toward presence and authority across the worlds.
studies.simplePa: ਛੰਦ ਪੁੱਛਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਨੂੰ ਸੀਮਤ ਪਛਾਣਾਂ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਪੂਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਜਾਣੀਏ। ਧਰਮ-ਗ੍ਰੰਥ, ਦਿਸਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਨਿਸ਼ਾਨ ਅਤੇ ਪਰਿਵਾਰਕ ਮੁੱਢ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਹੱਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣ ਸਕਦੇ। ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਅਤੇ ਸੱਤਾ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Separate a limit on complete knowledge from rejection of study or respect.
study.closeReading: The first line names powerful sources of knowledge and still says that the Divine mystery is not fully known. The second then asks what method of outward identification would work when form, colour, caste and lineage do not fix the One. The third deepens the contrast by removing parentage and the cycle of birth and death. The final line is not simply another denial: it describes movement or ordering throughout the directions and recognition in the three worlds. The difficult phrase ਚੱਕ੍ਰ ਬੱਕ੍ਰ must remain visible as a translation problem rather than disappear behind a confident smooth sentence. A thoughtful reading can acknowledge the limits of a description while continuing to learn from it.
words: scriptural books beyond the Vedas in this context
manner or description in this provisional reading
the three worlds in traditional cosmic language
study.care: The exact syntax of ਚੱਕ੍ਰ ਬੱਕ੍ਰ remains provisional. Traditional world-language is not an empirical map. Limits of scriptural comprehension do not justify contempt for scriptures, communities or education.
study.reflection: Recall something important that you understand only partly. How can recognising that limit make your questions more careful?
study.teachBack: Identify the three kinds of limitation discussed before the last line, and explain why uncertainty about one phrase should be stated rather than concealed.

studies.simpleEn: The stanza widens praise to the entire imagined cosmos while returning to the distinction between the beginning of creation and the beginningless Divine. Its final line places making and dissolution within the same address.
studies.simplePa: ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਉਸਤਤ ਨੂੰ ਸਮੂਹ ਬ੍ਰਹਿਮੰਡ ਤੱਕ ਫੈਲਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਰਚਨਾ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਢ ਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਅਨਾਦਿ ਹੋਣ ਦਾ ਫ਼ਰਕ ਮੁੜ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਘੜਨ ਅਤੇ ਸਮੇਟਣ ਦੋਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਸੱਤਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਰੱਖਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Read the cosmic scale as a widening of praise without confusing poetry and measurement.
study.closeReading: The opening invokes fourteen worlds to enlarge the range of the address. The second line then names the source of that expanse as both primal and beginningless. The third accumulates descriptions of purity, completeness and limitlessness before the fourth joins self-existence with the shaping and dissolution of the universe. Notice the repeated establishing language in ਥਾਪਿਓ and ਥਾਪਿ, then the paired actions ਗੜਨ and ਭੰਜਨ. The passage is not merely a list of impressive titles; it continually links the vastness of creation with a source not enclosed by creation. The reflective task is to recognise that scale without pretending the verse supplies a laboratory model or a timetable of cosmic events.
study.care: Traditional cosmological imagery is not presented as scientific evidence. Purity is attributed to the Divine, not used to label communities or bodies as impure.
study.reflection: What changes in your priorities when you place a small concern within a much larger view of life?
study.teachBack: Explain why the Divine can be called ਆਦਿ and ਅਨਾਦਿ together, and identify the two complementary actions in the last line.

studies.simpleEn: Being beyond time and outward identity does not make the Divine description morally empty. The stanza joins freedom from limitation with dharam, the humbling of pride, resistance to wickedness and the gift of liberation.
studies.simplePa: ਕਾਲ ਅਤੇ ਬਾਹਰੀ ਪਛਾਣ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੋਣ ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਨੈਤਿਕਤਾ ਤੋਂ ਖਾਲੀ ਹੋਣਾ ਨਹੀਂ। ਛੰਦ ਇਸ ਬੇਹੱਦੀ ਨੂੰ ਧਰਮ, ਹੰਕਾਰ ਦੇ ਟੁੱਟਣ, ਦੁਸ਼ਟਤਾ ਦੇ ਵਿਰੋਧ ਅਤੇ ਮੁਕਤੀ ਦੀ ਦਾਤ ਨਾਲ ਜੋੜਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Follow the turn from what cannot limit the Divine to the ethical force of the final line.
study.closeReading: The first three lines repeatedly deny enclosure by time, place, material form, visible appearance or social classification. Yet the second line already names a positive relationship to ਧਰਮ. The final line makes that relationship more concrete by bringing pride, wickedness and liberation into view. Pay attention to the way similar-looking vocabulary changes with its context: ਕਾਮ here is provisionally understood as work or function, not as the desire denied elsewhere. Likewise, ਅੰਗ ਰਾਗ can be read as a compound concerning adornment or analysed into separate terms. These choices belong in the notes, not in a silent alteration of the source. Ethical reflection can begin with pride in oneself rather than a licence to brand other people as enemies.
words: the humbling or breaking of pride
work or function in the selected contextual reading
study.care: No person receives a mandate here to punish those they call wicked. The selected readings of ਅਦੇਸ, ਅਭੂਤ and ਅੰਗ ਰਾਗ remain subject to qualified review; the Divine attributes are not guarantees of human invulnerability.
study.reflection: Where might pride make it harder for you to admit harm, apologise or change course?
study.teachBack: Describe the stanza’s movement toward the final ethical line, and explain why ਕਾਮ should not be given the same meaning in every passage.

studies.simpleEn: Depth beyond complete praise is joined to freedom from birth and bodily limits. The stanza also repeats the demanding pair of dissolution and nurture. Its difficult vocabulary asks for humility from the interpreter as well as from the reader.
studies.simplePa: ਪੂਰੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਡੂੰਘਾਈ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਜਨਮ ਅਤੇ ਸਰੀਰਕ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੋਣਾ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸਮੇਟਣ ਅਤੇ ਪਾਲਣ ਦਾ ਔਖਾ ਜੋੜ ਵੀ ਮੁੜ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਮੁਸ਼ਕਲ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਪੜ੍ਹਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਆਖਿਆ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਦੋਵਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਮੰਗਦੇ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Let the limits of praise also limit overconfident interpretation.
study.closeReading: The stanza begins with its own restraint: the One being praised is deeper than the praise can contain. That restraint matters when reaching ਅਨਾਤਮ, a term that should not be assigned a familiar modern slogan without argument. The working explanation keeps its relation to the neighbouring denials of bodily limitation and its affirmations of oneness and boundlessness. The last line then prevents a purely abstract reading by returning to power, ending and nurture. These are not qualities owned by a human speaker. A careful learner can understand the main direction of the stanza while also identifying which particular words need a qualified reader’s attention. Uncertainty made explicit is more useful than a falsely definitive glossary.
words: not a limited personal self in this provisional interpretation
study.care: The ਅਨਾਤਮ and ਲਾਇਕ explanations are provisional, not settled scholarly translations. Bodilessness does not devalue disability or embodied life; descriptions of ending life never authorise personal violence.
study.reflection: Where could saying “this is my working understanding” make a conversation more truthful and more open?
study.teachBack: Explain the opening limit on praise, name the difficult term in line three, and show how the last line holds ending and nurture together.

studies.simpleEn: This stanza returns to the limits of description after praising presence, ending and freedom from outward guise. Accumulating more words does not give the mind possession of the unlimited, though study can still deepen understanding and humility.
studies.simplePa: ਵਿਆਪਕਤਾ, ਅੰਤ ਅਤੇ ਭੇਸ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਛੰਦ ਵਰਣਨ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਦਾ ਹੈ। ਹੋਰ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਜੋੜ ਲੈਣ ਨਾਲ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਮਨ ਦੀ ਮਲਕੀਅਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣ ਜਾਂਦਾ, ਪਰ ਪੜ੍ਹਾਈ ਸਮਝ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਡੂੰਘਾ ਕਰ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Understand the limits of language without making ignorance a virtue.
study.closeReading: The opening line continues the poem’s comprehensive address through ਸਰਬ twice, then refuses confinement to a guise. The remaining three lines examine the means by which a reader might try to define that reality: teachings, revered books and the mind itself. ਨੇਤਿ interrupts the wish to identify one final description with the whole. The last line increases the imagined quantity of texts, yet still does not promise complete mental possession. This movement should not be used to excuse careless interpretation. On the contrary, recognising the limits of language gives the learner reason to distinguish what the words say, what a commentary proposes and what remains uncertain. The stanza closes the Rooaal sequence before the separate heading at 87.
words: going or reaching in this working reading
not confined to an outward guise
a refusal of final identification: not this, not that
a very large number; here an intensifier
study.care: The limits of complete knowledge do not discredit education, evidence or reason. The explanation of ਨੇਤਿ is contextual and introductory, not a claim that all traditions use the term identically.
study.reflection: What is one place where you could study carefully while letting go of the need to sound certain about everything?
study.teachBack: Explain the progression from sacred teachings to the mind, and why the final line is not a command to stop reading.

studies.simpleEn: After the long Rooaal lines, the Madhubhaar heading brings a compact sequence of virtues, boundless greatness, an unbreakable seat and praise beyond comparison. Shorter lines still carry distinct images that deserve separate attention.
studies.simplePa: ਰੂਆਲ ਦੀਆਂ ਲੰਮੀਆਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਮਧੁਭਾਰ ਸਿਰਲੇਖ ਹੇਠ ਗੁਣਾਂ, ਬੇਅੰਤ ਮਹਿਮਾ, ਅਟੁੱਟ ਆਸਣ ਅਤੇ ਤੁਲਨਾ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਉਸਤਤ ਦੀਆਂ ਛੋਟੀਆਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਆਉਂਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਛੋਟੀਆਂ ਹੋਣ ਦੇ ਬਾਵਜੂਦ ਹਰ ਤੁਕ ਆਪਣਾ ਵੱਖਰਾ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਰੱਖਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Notice the change of form without losing the four separate images.
study.closeReading: The heading is separate from the four source lines and marks the transition to Madhubhaar. The first pair names virtues and then the impossibility of measuring greatness. The second pair offers a firm seat while again resisting a bounded comparison. That alternation matters: a concrete image such as a throne helps the imagination, but the next line prevents the image from becoming a complete definition. Read ਆਸਨ as imagery before assuming it is an instruction about the reader’s body. The final phrase also needs interpretive modesty; the beauty emphasis and the beyond-bodily-comparison reading should remain distinguishable. The form becomes compact, not simplistic.
words: an abundance or gathering of virtues
beyond bodily limitation in this provisional reading
study.care: No human ruler inherits an unbreakable throne from this image. The final phrase remains a working interpretation, and the metrical heading receives no extra verse credit.
study.reflection: When an image helps you understand something, how do you remember that the image is not the whole reality?
study.teachBack: Identify the new metrical heading, explain why it is separate, and contrast the concrete seat image with the limits of comparison.

studies.simpleEn: Self-revealing light and enduring presence are followed by a heroic image and supreme sovereignty. The stanza shifts between descriptions beyond physical limits and an image drawn from bodily majesty without requiring the image to be literal anatomy.
studies.simplePa: ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਤੋਂ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਅਤੇ ਅਵਿਨਾਸ਼ੀ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਵੀਰਤਾ ਦਾ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਅਤੇ ਪਰਮ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹੀ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਛੰਦ ਸਰੀਰਕ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਰੀਰਕ ਮਹਾਨਤਾ ਦੇ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਨਾਲ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ; ਇਸ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਨੂੰ ਸ਼ਾਬਦਿਕ ਸਰੀਰ ਮੰਨਣਾ ਲਾਜ਼ਮੀ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: Hold the long-armed image beside the poem’s earlier freedom from bodily limits.
study.closeReading: The first two lines address the source of light and the persistence of the One through the changing cycle of night and day. The third changes the kind of language being used: far-reaching arms offer an image of majesty and capacity. Earlier lines have denied confinement to bodily limbs, so the image should be read within the whole poem rather than used to cancel those denials. The final sovereign title raises the scale beyond any individual ruler. A learner can therefore ask two different questions: what image is being offered, and what claim would go too far if the image were made literal? The distinction protects both the force of the poetry and honesty about interpretation.
words: self-revealing light in the selected reading
a traditional long-armed image of majesty
study.care: No light vision, bodily characteristic or spiritual experience is required for a person to belong or practise. The different interpretations of ਅਨਭਉ and ਆਜਾਨ remain visible rather than being presented as settled.
study.reflection: Think of a metaphor that gives you courage. How could you keep its meaning without insisting it must describe a literal event?
study.teachBack: Explain why the arm image need not contradict earlier bodilessness language, and distinguish the sovereign title from a breath-related reading.

studies.simpleEn: Rulers, suns and gods become points of comparison, and each comparison points beyond itself. The final line gathers these images into praise rather than treating any finite authority, brilliance or heavenly power as the final limit.
studies.simplePa: ਰਾਜੇ, ਸੂਰਜ ਅਤੇ ਦੇਵਤੇ ਤੁਲਨਾ ਦੇ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਬਣਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਹਰ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਆਪਣੇ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਦੀ ਮਹਾਨਤਾ ਵੱਲ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਇਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਉਸਤਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਜੋੜਦੀ ਹੈ; ਕੋਈ ਸੀਮਤ ਸੱਤਾ, ਚਾਨਣ ਜਾਂ ਦੇਵਤਾ ਅੰਤਿਮ ਹੱਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਦਾ।

study.focus: Recognise the repeated pattern of surpassing comparison.
study.closeReading: The first three lines use a similar verbal construction while changing the comparison: political power, visible brilliance and heavenly authority. None is dismissed as an empty word, yet none is allowed to set the final scale. The fourth line names praise and greatness, making the function of the comparisons more apparent. This way of reading can help the learner avoid two extremes: reducing the lines to a literal ranking chart, or flattening all three into a vague statement that the Divine is great. Keep the distinct images first, then ask how each is exceeded. The result is a widening of reverence, not a warrant for human domination.
words: the Divine revered beyond the gods
study.care: Solar language is poetic, not a scientific explanation. Political and divine titles do not confer absolute authority on any person, institution or state.
study.reflection: Which kind of human greatness most easily captures your attention—power, brilliance or reputation—and what helps you keep it in proportion?
study.teachBack: Name the three kinds of comparison and explain what the final line tells you about their purpose.

studies.simpleEn: The stanza reaches from heavenly sovereignty and exalted rank to the poorest person, then beyond death. Its change of direction matters: greatness is not confined to prestige, and the presence of the Divine is not measured by wealth.
studies.simplePa: ਛੰਦ ਦੇਵਤਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਰਾਜਾਈ ਅਤੇ ਉੱਚੇ ਮਾਣ ਤੋਂ ਗਰੀਬਾਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਗਰੀਬ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਦਾ ਹੈ, ਫਿਰ ਕਾਲ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਮੋੜ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਹੈ: ਵਡਿਆਈ ਕੇਵਲ ਰੁਤਬੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੱਝੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਧਨ ਨਾਲ ਨਹੀਂ ਤੋਲੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ।

study.focus: Notice how the line about poverty interrupts a simple ladder of rank.
study.closeReading: The repeated construction might initially sound like a steady ascent through higher and higher titles. The third line disrupts that expectation with ਰੰਕਾਨ ਰੰਕ. The final line then goes beyond the ordinary categories of rank by addressing death itself. The second line also requires an explicit interpretive choice. This draft uses the exalted sense supported by the ਬਾਲਾ lexical comparison and the consulted commentary, while preserving the different smallness or child reading found elsewhere. Do not hide that difference behind a single polished sentence. Whatever reading receives eventual qualified approval, the poor must not disappear from the stanza. Reflection can attend to the dignity of someone with little social power while still recognising the hardship of deprivation.
words: higher than the highest in the selected reading; alternatives retained
beyond death or the death of death
study.care: The ਬਾਲਾਨ ਬਾਲ reading needs qualified Sikh/Punjabi review. Poverty is not proof of virtue or fault, and it should not be romanticised. The final line promises no bodily immortality.
study.reflection: Who might be overlooked because they lack status or money, and what respectful, practical action would recognise their dignity?
study.teachBack: Explain the selected and alternative readings of the second line, then describe how the third line changes the direction of the stanza.
